doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
title: The Benghazi and watching Roy Haynes with Lester Young
summary: Cobb remembers peering into the Benghazi through a smoke fan to see Roy Haynes with Pres.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I’m trying to think about some other places around there. There was the Benghazi, because I remember – there was a place right on T Street, right on the corner. What was that? I remember seeing Roy Haynes in there with Pres [Lester Young], because the bandstand, you could – the bandstand faced where there was a fan – smoke fan that was blowing the [?] out.
This is the same – Benny Caldwell had that place too. He had that place, and he had the Caverns. I don’t know why I’m stuck on stupid . . .

Yeah, right on the corner. I used to go there. They had a little stairs that looked like a side entrance or something. I used to climb up on this, look through the fan, with smoke blowing in my face, at the bandstand, at Roy Haynes playing with Pres. I tell him about that too. He tried to say that was him looking at me, you see, because I met him a few times before when he came down. He just came down there – the first time I saw him, he was with a house band from Boston that he worked with. I keep – the name keeps coming up, and I keep forgetting it, but it was a Boston house band that he came down there with. Then, the next time I saw him, I think he came down with Pres. Then I think later on he was with Sarah Vaughan. Then he was with Bird [Charlie Parker]. He was with – he was all over the place. He was doing very good. So I met him. I’ve been knowing him 60 years or something like that. He was always nice. He would always talk to me, and it was always friendly like that. I remember that. He’s still like that. A good man. I can never think of that band up there, but it was a big thing.
I know I’ve seen him associated with – that was an important Boston guy, not the only thing, but it seemed like . . .
Sabby Lewis or something like that.
Sabby Lewis. That’s what it is.
Something like that. I remember vaguely something like that.
